THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY,
 THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 -2-  CRL.P No. 101215 of 2023  ORDER Heard Sri.Iranagouda K Kabbur, learned counsel for the petitioner and learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent - State.

2. This petition is filed under Section 438 of Cr.P.C., with the following prayer:
"The petition may be allowed and the petitioner/accused No.1 may be granted anticipatory bail in Ballari Women PS.
Crime No. 026/2023 registered for the offence P/u/sec. 498A, 323, 504, 506 R/w 34 of IPC and Sec. 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act 1961."

3. Brief facts of the case are as under:
3.1 Wife of the petitioner lodged a complaint with Ballari WomEn Police on 08.02.2023 which was registered in Crime No.26/2023 for the offence punishable under Sections 498A, 504, 323, 506 read with 34 OF IPC.
3.2

Gist of the complaint averments reveal that the complainant has been married to the petitioner herein on 09.10.2015 as per the Muslim rights and rituals and at the time of marriage ten tola gold and other household articles were given as dowry.

Thereafter, the complainant jointed the matrimonial home and led a happy marital life for a brief period of two months and thereafter the petitioner herein addicted to bad vices and started consuming unlimited liquor and under the influence of liquor was harassing the complainant both physically and mentally and also demanded dowry.
3.3 It is also alleged that by administering medicines to the complainant, the petitioner was responsible for abortion for eight times and therefore lodged a complaint.
Police after registering the case are investigating the matter and petitioner is not available to the investigating agency.

sentences.text: 4. The attempt made by the petitioner to obtain an order of grant of bail was turned down by the learned District Judge in Crl.Misc. No.121/2023 by order dated 14.03.2023.
Thereafter, the petitioner is before this Court.

5. Reiterating the grounds urged in the petition, Sri.Iranagouda K Kabbur, learned counsel for the petitioner vehemently contended that the allegations found in the complaint are per se false and the petitioner is innocent of the offences alleged against him and sought for grant of anticipatory bail.
6. Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader opposes the grounds urged in the petition.
7. In view of the rival contentions of the parties, this Court has perused the material on record meticulously.
8. On such perusal, it is seen that in the year 2015 marriage between the petitioner and the complainant has taken place.
According to the complainant there are eight times where abortion took place by administering medicines to the complainant by the petitioner.
How anybody would remain in the husband's house if such an atrocity has taken place is a question that has to be investigated by the investigating agency.

Taking note of the principles of law enunciated by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Arnesh Kumar vs. State of Bihar reported in (2014) 8 SCC 273, in a matter of this nature, the police are required to have a delegate approach with regard to the allegations made in the complaint so as to find out if the marriage could be saved.

entities.text: Arnesh Kumar vs. State of Bihar reported in (2014) 8 SCC 273
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 9. Keeping in mind, all these aspects of the matter, directing the petitioner to join the investigation by appearing before the investigating officer and undergo limited period of custodial interrogation, would meet the ends of justice.
10. Accordingly without further discussion on the merits of the matter, following order is passed:

ORDER The criminal petition is allowed subject to the following conditions:
1. The Petitioner is directed to join the investigation by appearing before the Investigating Officer on 28.06.2023 at 10.00 a.m.

2. The Investigating Officer is at liberty to take the petitioner to custody and complete the custodial interrogation, if any, on the same day before 6.00 p.m. and thereafter enlarge the petitioner on bail by taking a bond in a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees one lakh only) with two sureties for the likesum to the satisfaction of the Investigating Officer.
Mohammaed

4. The petitioner shall attend the Court regularly.

5. The petitioner shall mark his attendance before the Investigating Officer on every 3rd Sunday between 10.00 a.m. to 2.00 p.m., till the final report is filed.
6.
The petitioner shall not directly or indirectly tamper the prosecution evidence or hamper the investigation process in any manner.

Violation of any one of the conditions would entitle the prosecution to seek for cancellation of bail.
Ordered accordingly.
